remaining_concerns: The affected multilingual customer support segment remains exposed in the initial rollout while below target on Spanish-language refund guidance.
There is still no completed approved risk acceptance covering the exposed multilingual customer support segment.
The actor's narrower position supports, at most, a conditional certification theory; the current record does not establish that the required disclosure predicate has been satisfied.
There is still no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been drafted, reviewed, approved, and included in the launch package before launch.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and instead reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is substantively more defensible than an unconditional certification claim, but it does not close the initial compliance predicates. Admissible evidence still shows: the release passed aggregate readiness and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents; the multilingual customer support segment remains exposed and below target on Spanish-language refund guidance; the rollout controls do not exclude that affected use case; the risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and does not cover the exposure; and policy requires disclosure unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch. The key distinction is between a caveated theory of what could be compliant if disclosure were actually completed, versus evidence that compliance has already been established. On this record, the latter is still missing, so `compliant_with_caveats` is not supported.
